correctness.rationale: Condition on side distance; prove the exact acute-angle wedge and latitude inequality; integrate to derive conditional probability A(d); evaluate two square-root corrections via the substitutions x=sin(d/2), x²=sin²t+cos(2t)sin²phi. This gives the precise M0 and M1, with full boundary coverage d<pi/2. Isotropic tensor averaging and antipodal parity yield the exact all-dipole law; normalized Fisher expansions yield pinned and three-iid coefficients. Companion verify.py midpoint quadrature and fixed-seed stochastic checks corroborate, but do not constitute proof.

originality.rationale: The uniform spherical acute probability is explicitly acknowledged as classical, especially Maeda 2008. A full reading of the related 2013 Li/Cooper/Eum paper identifies only an unweighted integral and numerical pinned Fisher curve. Neither that work nor accessible metadata of Maeda and Le gives the new weighted cosine value, exact dipole law or Fisher slope. Primary-source comparisons and targeted literature searches found no dominating implication; full historic texts not obtained and originality remains provisional.
residual_risks: The full 2008 Maeda article was not retrievable; its uniform type table definitely covers M0 but other content is not ruled out.
The full 1989 Le cap-shape-density article was not retrieved; a weighted moment could in principle be derived from broader work.
An earlier equivalent nonuniform sampling result could exist outside indexed sources. Search absence is not a uniqueness proof.
No independent literature/prior-art audit was conducted.

value.rationale: The exact weighted moment solves a concrete directional-nonuniform extension of a classical random spherical triangle problem, connects to the pinned Fisher experiment that previously reported only a numerical onset, and by a tensor cancellation yields the entire nontrivial dipole probability at every admissible parameter. This is motivated by a natural directional density and is not merely a rephrasing of the known uniform acute probability.
